name: Qualtrics
oneLiner: Enterprise experience management (XM) platform for customer, employee and brand research, with location CX dashboards, an online reputation management module and AI Experience Agents.
bestFor: Large, multi-unit restaurant and hospitality brands with dedicated CX or insights teams that want surveys, reviews and operational feedback in one enterprise program.

updates.text: At X4 2026 (Seattle, March 17-19), new CEO Jason Maynard's first X4, Qualtrics said its AI Experience Agents are live with paying customers and announced real-time service recovery agents and omnichannel connectors for Genesys, NICE and Salesforce.
Qualtrics completed its $6.75 billion acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta (announced October 2025), adding healthcare patient-experience data and the InMoment business Press Ganey had bought in 2025.

features: Omnichannel feedback collection: post-transaction surveys by email, SMS, web, app, QR and chat
Online reputation management that aggregates reviews from sites such as Google, Yelp, Facebook and TripAdvisor alongside survey data
AI response suggestions that match the brand's voice, with replies sent from Qualtrics dashboards (Google Places and Facebook connections)
Location CX dashboards with role-based views for restaurant managers, market managers and executives
AI text and sentiment analytics that group open-ended comments and reviews into themes
Experience Agents: AI agents that act on feedback, for example real-time service recovery
Predictive analytics on drivers of satisfaction and churn risk
Brand research (BrandXM) and employee experience programs on the same platform
Connectors to contact-center and CRM systems such as Genesys, NICE and Salesforce

pricing.text: Custom pricing. The pricing page lists CX plans, including one for location-based industries such as restaurants, hotels and retail, each with 'Request Pricing' and no price. CX pricing is based on interactions (data records collected or processed by Qualtrics). No free trial or free plan is listed; the page leads to a demo.

notes: Dropped from the current review: 'starts at approximately $50,000-$100,000+ per year' and 'pricing based on customer interactions' (not published by Qualtrics). 'Government institutions' and ServiceNow as customers not re-verified; Shake Shack confirmed. KFC figures (300% more feedback, ~30-32K restaurants) are vendor-published. The Press Ganey deal is mainly healthcare; it does not change the restaurant offering. Qualtrics is privately held (taken private by Silver Lake in 2023). X4 2026 details come from press coverage, not a Qualtrics release. 2026-11: the pricing page (qualtrics.com/pricing) was opened: no prices, 'Request Pricing' on every CX plan, CX priced by interactions, no free trial listed. The ORM product page (qualtrics.com/customer-experience/reputation-management/) says it 'generates response suggestions that match your brand voice' and lets users reply from dashboards; the support page limits dashboard replies to Google Places and Facebook connections. G2 rating (4.3, 751 reviews) is from G2 search result snippets; g2.com returned 403.
pros: Surveys, public reviews, brand research and employee programs on one platform
AI response suggestions in the brand's voice, with replies sent from Qualtrics dashboards
Location dashboards scoped by role, from restaurant manager to executive
Experience Agents that act on feedback, including real-time service recovery
Predictive analytics on what drives satisfaction and churn
Large restaurant references: KFC and Shake Shack
Rated 4.3/5 on G2 (Qualtrics Customer Experience, 751 reviews)

cons.text: No published prices: every CX plan says 'Request Pricing', and CX pricing is based on interactions
No free trial or free plan listed; buying starts with a demo request
Built for enterprise programs run by CX or insights teams, so a small restaurant group may pay for more platform than it uses
Replying from dashboards works for reviews connected through Google Places or Facebook, and only for users with read and reply access to the project
Reviews are one module of a broad research suite; review-reply volume and speed are not its main focus

plans.billing: custom quote; CX pricing is based on interactions
